questions.q: The elder generation often has valuable insights based on their life experiences.
questions.s:
When referring to age within a generational context, "older" is more appropriate than "elder."

    • "Elder" is typically used for individuals (e.g., my elder brother), not for groups or generations.
    • "Older generation" is the correct phrase when referring to a previous generation as a whole.

So, the corrected sentence would be: "The older generation often has valuable insights based on their life experiences."

Why "has" (Singular) and "their" (Plural) are both correct?

"The older generation" is singular:

  • The word "generation" refers to a collective group, but grammatically, it is treated as a singular noun.
  • Since "generation" is singular, we use "has" instead of "have."

"Their" is used for collective possession:

  • Even though "generation" is singular, it represents many people within that generation.
  • In modern English, "their" is often used as a gender-neutral pronoun for groups of people.

Here, "their life experiences" refers to the experiences of multiple individuals within the older generation.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

This is the ______ book that I have read till now.
questions.s:
It can be noted that the sentence is in the superlative degree, signifying that the book that is mentioned in the sentence is ultimate amongst all the books the subject has read so far. So, the superlative adjective "most interesting" is appropriate for comparing the book to all others read, indicating it is the best in terms of interest.

The complete sentence: This is the most interesting book that I have read till now.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
o: We have not received
our coast guards yet
some information from
questions.s:
Solution:

  • The sentence is:
    "We have not received some information from our coast guards yet."

  • The error lies in the phrase: "some information from"

  • Explanation:

  • When used in negative sentences, we typically use "any" instead of "some".

  • "Some" is generally used in affirmative sentences, while "any" fits naturally with negatives and questions.

  • Therefore, the correct phrase should be: "We have not received any information..."

  • Why the other options are correct:

  • "We have not received" – grammatically correct.

  • "our coast guards yet" – correctly placed and used.

  • "No error" – incorrect because an error exists in the sentence.

Corrected sentence:
"We have not received any information from our coast guards yet."

Hence, option (c) is correct.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.
